title: Female borrowers who express explicit gratitude in their pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention their dreams or aspirations fund faster.
Female borrowers who express direct gratitude to lenders may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention contributing to food production in their community may fund faster.
Female borrowers mentioning a general store business may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who describe fleeing political instability, such as in South Sudan, may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention being married or providing for family may fund faster than those who are single or widowed.
Male borrowers who specify exact quantities of assets or livestock may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their specific age in the pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide specific numbers for age and children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who explicitly name their institutional partner fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention family members or household responsibilities fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who specify concrete educational or institutional goals for their children fund faster.
